# `role_needs_invalid`: a crash declaration or crash branch is missing or misplaced

`may crash C` says role `C` may fail mid-conversation. From then on,
every receive from `C` needs an `or crash do ... end` branch that says how the
conversation goes on without `C`. A crash branch on a receive from a role that
is not declared `may crash` is refused too, and so is a `choose` whose crash
branch has no single role to detect the crash. The message says which rule
applies. When it can, `march --check` also offers a fix you can apply.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs Session.Live

  @[endpoints]
  protocol Logging do
    may crash C
    L -> I : Int
    C -> I : String
    I -> L : String
  end

  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do () end
end
```

`C` may crash, but the receive `C -> I : String` does not say what `I`
does if `C` crashes before sending.

## The fix

Add a crash branch to the receive. Its steps are the rest of the
conversation when `C` is gone:

```march
mod Main do
  needs IO
  needs Session.Live

  @[endpoints]
  protocol Logging do
    may crash C
    L -> I : Int
    C -> I : String
      or crash do
        I -> L : String
      end
    I -> L : String
  end

  fn main(c : Cap(IO)) do () end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

A receive from a role that may crash can wait forever. The crash branch
makes the receiver's next step explicit, and the checks on where it may appear
keep every remaining role in agreement about which path the conversation
took.

See also: [when a role may crash](../choreography.md#when-a-role-may-crash).
